title: 'Each player must kill one of their units' resolves as a single choose-target prompt for the controller over ALL units (friendly and enemy), killing exactly one unit total.
expected: Parser emits {type:"kill", player:"each", target:{type:"unit"}} (riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/effects-damage.ts:139-150). The engine never honours player:"each" for kill: game-definition/moves/chain/resolve.ts:160-241 builds a single choose-target for resolved.controller with options = resolveTarget({type:"unit", quantity:"all"}) — no controller filter, so all friendly+enemy units — and remaining:1; abilities/effects/kill.ts handle_kill (lines 8-37) just kills the bound target(s) with no per-player fan-out (unlike discard.ts:18/draw.ts:10/channel.ts:13 which do branch on player==="each"). Result: controller picks one unit from any side, one kill total; opponent never kills their own unit.
observed: pendingChoice {type:choose-target, playerId:player-1, remaining:1, options:[Gem Jammer(p1), Safety Inspector(p1), Recruit token(p2)]}. After p1 picked Gem Jammer, effect ended: p2's Recruit survived, no prompt/auto-kill for player-2. In a second run p1 was able to pick and kill p2's Recruit token instead.

history.note: each-player kill already fans out per player; locked options to the chooser's own units in the repro test
